moved.sentence: Before committing to an architecture, ask: "What would it cost to reverse this in six months?"

judged.note: The rule keeps at SHOULD asking, before committing to an architecture, what it would cost to reverse it in six months.

moved.sentence: Prefer decisions that keep options open over decisions that lock in a technology or pattern

judged.note: The rule keeps at SHOULD preferring decisions that keep options open over ones that lock in a technology or pattern.

moved.sentence: When two approaches are otherwise equal, choose the one that is easier to change later

moved.sentence: Treat **cognitive load** as the metric the structural principles serve: simplicity, locality of behavior, and boundaries all exist to reduce the cognitive load of understanding and changing the system, so a design — or an agent workflow — **SHOULD** be tested by whether it lowers that load.

judged.note: should-test-design-by-cognitive-load keeps cognitive load as the metric and the SHOULD test of a design or agent workflow; rationale keeps that simplicity, locality of behavior and boundaries exist to reduce that load.

moved.sentence: Caveat: AI and multi-agent tooling can *shift* load onto the human orchestrator rather than remove it, so use cognitive load as a lens (proxies: fan-out, file count, time-to-onboard), not a thresholded metric.

judged.note: should-use-cognitive-load-as-a-lens keeps the lens-not-threshold instruction with its proxies, and rationale keeps the caveat that AI and multi-agent tooling can shift load onto the human orchestrator.
